headline: A Democratic sweep in the US midterms sends Treasuries lower in Asian hours and foreigners buy 14,000 3Y futures: KTBs rally across the curve, 3Y −2.2bp to 3.714% (a three-month low) and 10Y −3.3bp to 3.968%
summary: KTBs rallied for a second day, led by 5Y and longer: 5–20Y fell 3.3bp, 30Y −3.6bp to 4.053% and 50Y −3.9bp to 4.076%, while the 3Y fell 2.2bp to 3.714% and the 1Y only 0.6bp to 3.578%. The 10Y closed below 4% at 3.968% and 3s10s flattened another 1.1bp to 25.4bp, a fresh 1-year low. The front end stayed pinned by November hike pricing: MSB 91-day held at 3.182% (98th percentile) and CD 91-day dipped 1bp to 3.34% from its high, but CP rose to 3.83%, so CP–CD widened to 49bp. KDB held about 28bp over KTB at 1–3Y, AAA bank 1Y about 43bp over (95th percentile) and AA- 3Y 69bp over, all still wide; KEPCO 3Y at 44bp is near its 1-year wide.
drivers: US midterms: Treasuries rally in Asia

Early counts pointed to Democratic control of both chambers, US equity futures fell and the US 10Y dropped about 5bp to near 4.90% during the Seoul session. That was the main catalyst for the across-the-board KTB rally, and the move faded slightly in the afternoon as the initial reaction was pared.
US Treasuries: the close says sell-off, Asia said rally

On the official New York close (before the vote count) the US 10Y par yield rose about 4bp to 4.95% on a strong JOLTS (7.52m vs 7.13m expected) and oil swings. At the 1-year daily beta of 0.45 that implied a 1.8bp KTB sell-off; the 10Y instead fell 3.3bp, so the close-to-close model books about −5bp as local. Roughly 2bp of that is the Asia-hours Treasury rally at the same beta, the rest local demand. The KTB–UST 10Y gap widened to −98bp, a new 1-year extreme.

Foreigners bought a net 14,033 3Y KTB futures and 393 10Y contracts, after buying 10Y futures on Tuesday, adding to downward pressure on yields. On our basket valuation 3Y fair value rose 7 ticks to 103.70 and 10Y 33 ticks to 108.52; we did not find KRX settles in the wraps, so no basis read today.

KOSPI swung about 400 points (high 5,828, low 5,422) before closing +0.62% at 5,683.80; foreigners sold KRW 2.51tn, a fourth straight day, while pension-led institutions (KRW 1.01tn) and individuals (KRW 1.14tn) bought. USD/KRW was little changed at 1,341.5 and October FX reserves rose USD 2.6bn to USD 443.2bn.
data: Highest since May 2022; supports the won, no direct KTB impact.
In line to a touch soft; the fuel price cap flatters headline, so it does not rule out a November 26 hike.
Strong end-user demand; the 30Y now trades 1.7bp below the auction yield.
Trade strength underpins the won and the BOK's hawkish lean.
Fastest output gain since 2011; keeps hike pricing in the 1–2Y.
Large beat on chip capex and government spending; private consumption fell 0.2%.
Hold at 3.00%, unanimous (after +25bp in July and August)
Guided to staying restrictive; a November 26 hike to 3.25% remains the front-end base case.
view: The rally extended for global reasons today, but the bigger picture is still local: over four weeks the 10Y is −43bp, of which about −20bp is US Treasuries at a weekly beta of 0.59 and −23bp is Korea's own equity-to-bond rotation, and the rotation signal held at +1.74 (bond rally) with foreigners selling stocks for a fourth day. With a November 26 hike still priced in the 1–3Y and US refunding, payrolls and a fresh 10Y supply week ahead, I expect the 10Y to hold 3.90–4.08% over the next two weeks and would not chase below 3.95%; I would buy a back-up toward 4.10%. The curve keeps grinding flatter against our 3s10s steepener (25.4bp, 0.4bp above the 25bp stop): I keep the stop where it is and will exit on a close below it rather than widen it. The 50Y-over-30Y switch and the KDB overweight stay. The rotation view still works best against Treasuries: hedged with about 0.6 × US 10Y, the live signal's rally calls hit 66% and sell-off calls 69% (48% and 57% outright), with a Sharpe of 1.27 against 0.95, so a beta-hedged KTB long is the cleaner expression.

buckets.name: KTB 1–2Y front end
buckets.why: The 2Y fell 1.4bp to 3.687% (73rd percentile of its 1-year range, average 3.36%) and the 1Y only 0.6bp to 3.578% (87th), so the front end lagged the rally. MSB 91-day is 3.182% (98th percentile) and 1s2s is 10.9bp (3rd percentile, average 31bp): the market still prices a November 26 hike.
buckets.call: No trigger hit. Add 2Y above 3.80%; fade rallies below 3.62%.

buckets.name: 3s10s curve
buckets.why: 3s10s flattened 1.1bp to 25.4bp, a new 1-year low (average 40bp), as the 10Y outran a 3Y anchored by hike pricing; it is 5.5bp flatter in a week. Our steepener from 29bp is 3.6bp against and 0.4bp from its 25bp stop. One 10Y future carries about 3.0 times the DV01 of a 3Y (KRW 86k vs 29k per bp).
buckets.call: Keep the 3s10s steepener (buy 3 × 3Y, sell 1 × 10Y futures) from 29bp; target 36bp, stop 25bp on a close. Open, 3.6bp against; exit if the stop is hit.

buckets.name: KTB 10Y outright
buckets.why: The 10Y at 3.968% is at the 52nd percentile of a 3.08–4.60% range (average 3.89%) and 43bp lower over four weeks. The KTB–UST gap of −98bp is the widest of the year, so Korea has already outperformed a lot, and today's move ran against the New York close.
buckets.call: Buy zone 4.10–4.15% not reached; keep it with a stop at 4.25%. Don't chase below 3.95%.

buckets.name: Ultra-long 30–50Y
buckets.why: 30s50s is +2.3bp, the 93rd percentile of the year (average −9.6bp); the switch from +2.5bp is 0.2bp in our favour as the 50Y rallied 3.9bp against 3.6bp for the 30Y. On Tuesday's trades the liquid 2052 KTB (22-9) traded about 7bp cheap to the fitted curve, while the low-coupon 2039 (19-6) was about 10bp rich.
buckets.call: Keep the 30Y into 50Y switch at +2.5bp; target −3bp, stop +6bp. Open, 0.2bp in favour.

buckets.name: KDB 1–3Y vs KTB
buckets.why: The KDB fit (14 trades) puts KDB about 28–29bp over KTB at 1–3Y; at 3Y that is the 93rd percentile against a 19bp average, about 3bp wider than our entry. KOFIA's own 1Y KDB quote is 33bp over (93rd percentile, average 23bp). KEXIM shows 46bp, but its fit uses only 3 trades, so treat it as low confidence.
buckets.call: Hold the overweight from ~26bp; take profit at 20bp, cut above 35bp. Open, about 3bp against.

buckets.name: AAA bank debentures and money market
buckets.why: AAA bank paper (39-trade fit) is 43bp over the 1Y KTB, the 95th percentile (average 30bp), though the 2–3Y part tightened 3–5bp today. CD dipped to 3.34% but CP rose to 3.83%, a 1-year high, so CP–CD widened 2bp to 49bp (97th percentile, average 28bp). IBK 1Y at 39bp over (16 trades) is a 1-year wide.
buckets.call: No change: prefer KDB over bank debentures; revisit bank paper once CP–CD falls below 35bp.

buckets.name: Corporate credit (AA- 3Y)
buckets.why: AA- 3Y fell 2.2bp to 4.40%, in step with the KTB, leaving the spread at 69bp (80th percentile, average 61bp); KEPCO 3Y is 44bp over (99th percentile). Spreads have held through the equity sell-off, and new corporate cash (SK Hynix funds buying card and capital bonds) is a support, but there is no equity turn to buy into yet.
buckets.call: Add AA- only above 75bp or once KOSPI holds a rebound for a week; no trigger hit.

ktb:3.note: Lowest since Aug 5; foreign futures buying

watch: Next: US quarterly refunding (Wed Nov 4, results Thu morning in Asia) and the final midterm count, Korea September current account (Thu Nov 5), US October payrolls (Fri Nov 6), US 3Y/10Y/30Y auctions (Nov 9, 10, 12), Korea November 1–10 exports around Nov 11, then the BOK meeting on Nov 26; a reversal of the election rally in Treasuries or a KOSPI rebound is the main risk.
